A probabilistic Turing machine (PTM) is a fixed multitape machine with two total ordinary transition tables. At each nonhalting transition a fresh independent fair bit selects the table. It is polynomial time if one fixed integer polynomial p bounds the number of transitions on every random branch on every input x by $p(|x|)$. This is a worst-case branch bound, using [[def-polynomial-time-verifier-and-reduction-interface]], not an expected-time bound.

For an input of length n, probabilities may be defined on the finite space $\Omega_n=\{0,1\}^{p(n)}$, giving every word mass $2^{-p(n)}$. A deterministic simulator uses bit j for transition j and ignores unused suffix bits after halting. Acceptance probability is the sum of masses of words giving acceptance. Independence has the finite-variable meaning of [[def-independence-of-finite-random-variables]]. The finite probability space is not itself storage charged to the machine.

Use the fixed multitape fair-bit probabilistic machine interface of [[def-probabilistic-polynomial-time-machine-interface]], with a read-only input tape and charged work tapes. Fix one access profile for each class. In the **sequential** profile, input and work-tape heads move locally, one cell per transition. In the **VMW random-access** profile, the machine has a fixed number of heads; each may move locally, stay put, or jump to an address delimited by two classical work-tape heads. A classical input query reads the addressed input symbol in one transition. If heads collide on a work tape so that its operation is not defined, that tape operation is omitted in that transition. These access profiles define distinct classes and are never silently identified. Time is the worst-case number of transitions on every branch. Sequential-profile space counts distinct visited work cells; VMW-profile space is the maximum work-head address visited on any branch. The read-only input is uncharged.

For a fixed profile and bound t, PrTIME(t) is the class of languages with a machine accepting with probability strictly greater than 1/2 on members and at most 1/2 on nonmembers; PrTISP(t,s) imposes both bounds. We write PrTIME_VMW and PrTISP_VMW when using the VMW random-access profile. Superscript A permits exact classical membership queries to A; writing each query and returning from it are charged, and the total query-string length is bounded by the machine's time. For the sequential profile, LCH_1=PrTIME(n) and LCH_(j+1)=PrTIME(n)^{LCH_j}. An LCH oracle is deterministic: the probabilistic machine's fair-bit branches are external to its oracle queries.

A formula for MajSAT has a fixed finite variable set and is accepted when at least half of all assignments satisfy it. MajMajSAT has two disjoint, ordered variable blocks; for at least half of outer assignments, the residual formula must be true on at least half of the inner assignments. We use at-least-half for both formula thresholds. These formula conventions are distinct from the strict machine threshold; the bounded-overhead tie-normalization result is proved separately in [[lem-qc-unbounded-error-tie-normalization]].

machine $C_t$ such that, on unary input $1^n$, the machine halts within
$O(t(n))$ steps and outputs the binary numeral $\operatorname{bin}(t(n))$.

The function $s$ is **space-constructible** when there exists a deterministic
machine $C_s$ such that, on unary input $1^n$, the machine halts while using
$O(s(n))$ tape cells and outputs the binary numeral $\operatorname{bin}(s(n))$.

we also require the evident size condition
$$ n\le t(n) $$
for large enough $n$, so that the budget is at least large enough to read an
input of length $n$.

The new machine first reads $R+2$ selector bits, rejecting only the all-zero selector. On every nonzero selector it simulates the original machine for at most $R$ steps using $R$ fresh bits, records its outcome, and consumes any unused suffix bits in a no-op state. On the zero selector it consumes all $R$ fresh bits and rejects. By [F3] this is a well-defined clocked procedure. There are exactly $2^{2R+2}$ equiprobable strings and exactly $(2^{R+2}-1)A$ accepting ones, so $p'=(1-2^{-(R+2)})p$.

If $p\le1/2$ then $p'<1/2$. If $p>1/2$, then $A\ge2^{R-1}+1$, so $p-1/2\ge2^{-R}$; because $p\le1$, $p'-1/2=(p-1/2)-p\,2^{-(R+2)}\ge2^{-R}-2^{-(R+2)}>0$. Thus strict majority is preserved and an original tie becomes a strict no-instance.

The new acceptance probability cannot equal one half: such equality would require the integer $A$ to equal $2^{2R+1}/(2^{R+2}-1)$, which is not an integer because its denominator is odd and greater than one. Since no tie remains, swapping accepting and rejecting labels makes the complement machine accept strictly above one half exactly on the original no-instances. The selector and padding add $2R+2$ transitions, so the overhead is $O(R(n))$.

Let $\mathbb B:=\{0,1\}$. A **binary encoding** of a set $X$ is an injective
function
$$ e:X\to\mathbb B^* $$
([[def-function]], [[def-injection-surjection-bijection]]).

Fix a symbol $\mathtt{mal}$ not belonging to $X$. A **total decoder** for $e$
is a function
$$ d:\mathbb B^*\to X\cup\{\mathtt{mal}\} $$
such that
$$ d(e(x))=x\quad(x\in X),\qquad d(w)=\mathtt{mal}\quad(w\notin e[X]). $$
Thus $\mathtt{mal}$ is exactly the output on malformed codes, and the decoder
is defined on every binary word, not only on words in the image of $e$.

The encoding $e$ is **effective** when such a total decoder is specified.

The encoding is **prefix-free** when no codeword is a proper prefix of another:
there do not exist distinct $x,y\in X$ and a nonempty binary word $u$ with
$e(y)=e(x)u$.

Let A be its accepting path count. Apply [A1] to the deterministic predicate “M accepts on x with random string y,” obtaining F_x(y,z) with exactly one z per accepting y and no z for a rejecting y; put k=|z|. Define ψ_x(y,z,v,w)=(v∧F_x(y,z))∨(¬v∧((∨_i z_i)∨w)), with one padding bit w. For each fixed y, the v=0 branch contributes 2^{k+1}−1 satisfying assignments of (z,w), while the v=1 branch contributes 2 iff y accepts. Therefore exactly A of the 2^{R(n)} blocks contribute one above half and the others one below half, so ψ has at least half satisfying assignments iff A≥2^{R(n)−1}; tie normalization makes this equivalent to M's strict-majority decision.

For L∈LCH₂, let its O(N)-time oracle machine use an LCH₁ oracle C₀. For every query q, use the explicit clock $R(|q|)=\max(T(|q|),1)$ for its C₀ decider, including ignored suffix bits. Replace each query q by a proposed answer bit and an R(|q|)-bit path w for the corresponding tie-free machine: use the original machine for answer yes and its complemented machine for answer no. The condition that w accepts and exactly $2^{R(|q|)-1}$ accepting paths precede it in lexicographic order holds for exactly one w iff the proposed answer is correct. Encode the adaptive transcript canonically with fixed zero padding. For each syntactically valid record and selected query index i, let r_i be the number of earlier accepting paths minus $2^{R(|q|)-1}$; its two path counts take O(N) time because the serialized query lengths sum to O(N) and the extra padded bit per empty query is constant. A nondeterministic index chooses one i, while padded invalid indices contribute zero, so sums over i add their Gap counts exactly. Products use pairs of independent path strings. Invalid syntax and a witness path that fails to accept contribute nonnegative indicator penalties. Hence G=bad+Σ_i(r_i²+invalid_i) is a nonnegative integer difference of two path counts in O(N) time, and G=0 exactly for a syntactically valid query/answer/witness list in which each proposed answer has its unique boundary-rank witness. If h=A−B for #P counts A,B, pad both path machines to exactly 2^P binary choice strings, branch on one fair bit, accept A on branch 0 and reject exactly the accepting B strings on branch 1. derivations.claim: After a branch halts, consume each remaining fair bit on two parallel dummy edges that merge into the same unchanged halted state. Thus every length-T random string corresponds to exactly one path, including the 2^{T−t} suffix choices after a t-step halt. M accepts with probability greater than one half exactly when the number of length-T accepting paths exceeds 2^{T−1}. Add the time t to every configuration; the resulting configuration graph is acyclic and has at most 2^{O(S+log T)} configurations.

For path counts of length L, choose q=⌈n^β⌉ checkpoints spaced at most ⌈L/q⌉ transitions apart. Sum over all checkpoint configurations and multiply the q segment-path counts. Each checkpoint uses O(S+log T) bits, so one level has at most 2^{O(qS)}=2^{O(n)} checkpoint tuples. Repeating this factorization a fixed r>α/β times reduces the segment length from T to O(1); ceilings alter each length by at most one, which is absorbed by choosing r with strict slack. Thus the accepting-path count is computed by a constant-depth arithmetic circuit of size 2^{O(n)}, with O(T) output bits.

Replace every arithmetic sum and product node by the circuits in [A1]. Fan-in, operand length and output length are bounded by 2^{O(n)} and O(T), respectively; the substitutions keep constant depth and total size 2^{O(n)}. Gate labels contain the machine configuration descriptors, checkpoint tuple, arithmetic-gate address and local circuit address, all using O(n) bits. The transition relation and direct one-step path predicates are decidable from these labels and the input in O(n) sequential time.

Convert each nonstrict MAJ gate to a strict threshold by appending one constant-one input when its original fan-in is even; for odd fan-in the thresholds already agree. Convert AND/OR to strict majority using N−1 constant zeros/ones, respectively. If the resulting fan-in is N and P is the next power of two, append ceil((P−N)/2) constant-one inputs. For N even the difference P−N is even and this preserves the strict threshold; for N odd it is odd and the added ones make the threshold x≥(N+1)/2, again exactly x>N/2. The fan-in is now P, so a linear-time probabilistic oracle machine chooses a predecessor uniformly with log₂P fair bits and queries whether it evaluates to 1. Use the Van Melkebeek–Watson quantum Turing-machine model. It has a read-only input tape containing $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ followed by blanks, a classical work tape and a quantum work tape, both initialized to zero, and a fixed finite number of heads. Input cells are not charged. Work-tape space is the maximum address visited by any classical or quantum work head on any branch; this is the source's tape convention, not circuit width. Classical heads may move locally or jump to an address computed on the classical work tape. Quantum operations act on the cells under the quantum heads and are either unitary gates or single-qubit computational-basis measurements. A classical finite control chooses the operations and operands from its state, classical/input symbols and previous measurement outcomes; choices do not depend on the quantum basis path.

The model has coherent quantum random access to the input: for a binary address $i$, a query applies $Q_x|i,b\rangle=|i,b\mathbin\oplus x_i\rangle$ to the address register and one answer qubit; under the source indexing, $x_i=0$ whenever $i>n$. The address register is part of the quantum work tape, and each query is one step. Each step's transition table and gate label are finite. For each unitary-matrix entry, its first $k$ bits in real and imaginary parts are deterministically computable in time polynomial in $k$. This amplitude condition is part of the input-access model, not a free arbitrary-real gate assumption.

For a promise problem $(Y,N)$, $\mathrm{BQTISP}(t,s)$ means there is such a machine using at most $O(t)$ steps and $O(s)$ maximum work-head address on every branch, accepting each $x\in Y$ with probability at least $2/3$ and each $x\in N$ with probability at most $1/3$. There is no requirement off the promise. Bounds maximize over all branches, including branches of probability zero. The time coordinate counts ordinary transitions, measurements and coherent input queries. It is a machine-transition model, with its classical comparison class $\mathrm{PrTISP}_{\rm VMW}$ defined using the matching VMW random-access profile in [[def-qc-unbounded-error-time-space-counting-model]].

Use the fixed multitape fair-bit probabilistic machine interface of [[def-probabilistic-polynomial-time-machine-interface]], with a read-only input tape and charged work tapes. In the **VMW random-access** profile, the machine has a fixed number of heads; each may move locally, stay put, or jump to an address delimited by two classical work-tape heads. A classical input query reads the addressed input symbol in one transition. If heads collide on a work tape so that its operation is not defined, that tape operation is omitted in that transition. These access profiles define distinct classes and are never silently identified. Time is the worst-case number of transitions on every branch. Sequential-profile space counts distinct visited work cells; VMW-profile space is the maximum work-head address visited on any branch. The read-only input is uncharged.

The function $t$ is **time-constructible** when there exists a deterministic
machine $C_t$ such that, on unary input $1^n$, the machine halts within
$O(t(n))$ steps and outputs the binary numeral $\operatorname{bin}(t(n))$.

machine $C_s$ such that, on unary input $1^n$, the machine halts while using
$O(s(n))$ tape cells and outputs the binary numeral $\operatorname{bin}(s(n))$.

we also require the evident size condition
$$ n\le t(n) $$

$$\eta_j=64^{-2}(64^2\eta_0)^{(3/2)^j}.$$

Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed spaces over the same scalar field. On the vector space
$\mathcal B(X,Y)$ of bounded linear operators, the operator norm of
[[def-operator-norm]] is a norm.

For compatible linear maps between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces,

$$\lVert ST\rVert\le \lVert S\rVert\,\lVert T\rVert.$$

For every such linear map $T$,

$$\lVert T^*T\rVert=\lVert T\rVert^2.$$

For an integer $d\ge 1$, the $d$-level register is the complex inner-product space $Q_d=\mathbb C^d$ with the standard pairing $\langle z,w\rangle_{\rm root}=\sum_{j<d}z_j\overline{w_j}$, linear in the first argument as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]] and [[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]. Its **computational basis** is the ordered standard basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]].

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$

For all vectors $x,y$ in a real or complex inner-product space,

$$|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\| ,$$

with equality if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent.

Write $\mathcal Q_n$ for the ordered tensor product of $n$ copies of the two-level register from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]], with $\mathcal Q_0=\mathbb C$. Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$. Each $g\in G$ has an arity $r(g)\ge1$ and a specified unitary $U_g:\mathcal Q_{r(g)}\to\mathcal Q_{r(g)}$. An operation model states which listed gates may be called and what access or cost is assigned to them; the matrix $U_g$ by itself is only the mathematical gate data.

For $n\ge0$, the circuit wire set is $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ in its displayed order and its state space is $\mathcal Q_n$. The computational basis word $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})$ is assigned slot $\operatorname{enc}_n(x)$ from [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]], so wire $0$ is the most significant bit and the empty register has its single basis vector in slot $0$.

A gate occurrence on the $n$ wires is a pair $(g,(w_0,\ldots,w_{r(g)-1}))$ with distinct wire labels $w_j\in[n]$; the tuple order is the input and output factor order of the local gate. A layer is a finite ordered list of gate occurrences whose wire supports are pairwise disjoint. A unitary circuit is a finite chronological list $L_1,\ldots,L_d$ of such layers, with $L_1$ applied first and $L_d$ last; $d=0$ is the empty circuit. Its input, output, and terminally measured wires are specified as ordered lists without repetitions in $[n]$. This syntax specifies finite data only; the semantic action of gates on the full register is defined separately.

For a gate occurrence $g=(\gamma,w)$ in a circuit on $\mathcal Q_n$, let $\widetilde U_g$ be the global embedding from [[lem-qc-local-gate-wire-embedding]]. For a layer $L_t=(g_1,\ldots,g_s)$, define
$$U_{L_t}:=\widetilde U_{g_s}\cdots\widetilde U_{g_1}.$$
For a circuit with chronological layers $L_1,\ldots,L_d$, define
$$U_C:=U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}.$$
The empty circuit and every empty layer denote the identity on $\mathcal Q_n$.

Fix a length-$n$ finite promise computation from [[def-qc-promise-computation-model]], with input $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, zero-initialized auxiliary register $|0^{a(n)}\rangle$, circuit unitary $U_{C_n}$, and ordered output-wire tuple $O_n$. Let $P_{O_n}$ be the tensor-factor permutation that moves $O_n$, in its declared order, to the front, and let $W_n$ be the ordered tuple of all remaining wires ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]). Set
$$\psi_x:=U_{C_n}(|x\rangle\otimes|0^{a(n)}\rangle),\qquad v_x:=\operatorname{coord}(P_{O_n}\psi_x).$$
Here coordinates are in the ordered computational basis, and the root inner product is linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). For $z\in\{0,1\}^{|O_n|}$ and $w\in\{0,1\}^{|W_n|}$, write $e_{z,w}$ for the corresponding product-basis vector and define
$$p_{C_n}(z\mid x):=\sum_{w\in\{0,1\}^{|W_n|}}\left|\langle P_{O_n}\psi_x,e_{z,w}\rangle_{\rm root}\right|^2.$$
The acceptance probability is
$$p_{C_n}(x):=\sum_{\substack{z\in\{0,1\}^{|O_n|}\\A_n(x,z)=1}}p_{C_n}(z\mid x).$$
Equivalently, if $E_{A,x}$ is the diagonal projection onto the basis vectors $(z,w)$ with $A_n(x,z)=1$, then $p_{C_n}(x)=\operatorname{Tr}(E_{A,x}v_xv_x^\dagger)$; the matrix adjoint is conjugate transpose in an orthonormal basis ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[cor-finite-dimensional-inner-product-spaces-have-orthonormal-bases]]).

These are finite sums. The definition itself does not assert normalization, positivity of the resulting operator expression, or a probability bound; those consequences are the purpose of [[thm-qc-output-acceptance-law-normalizes]]. No Dirac bra convention is used here: every amplitude uses the root pairing displayed above.

A promise problem $\Pi=(Y,N)$ belongs to **BQP in the QC14 model** when there exist a full-list uniform family $(C_n)$ and a polynomial-time acceptance predicate $A_n$ as in [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]] and [[def-qc-quantum-acceptance-probability]] such that, for every $x\in Y$,
$$p_{C_{|x|}}(x)\ge\frac23,$$
and for every $x\in N$,
$$p_{C_{|x|}}(x)\le\frac13.$$
By [[thm-qc-output-acceptance-law-normalizes]], $p_{C_n}(x)$ is the probability of the specified acceptance event and lies in $[0,1]$. No condition is imposed for $x\notin Y\cup N$ ([[def-promise-problem]]). The gate alphabet is exactly $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$; its matrix entries lie in $\mathbb Q(\zeta_8)=\mathbb Q(i,\sqrt2)$ as specified by [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]]. This definition does not assert a BQP-versus-classical separation, nor does it assert an unproved equivalence with another circuit-uniformity convention.

Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$ with maximum arity $k:=\max(\{r(g):g\in G\}\cup\{0\})$ and a circuit from [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]]. The declared **size** is the number of gate occurrences, equivalently $\sum_{t=1}^d|L_t|$; the declared **depth** is the number $d$ of explicit layers, not a minimum over alternate layerings; the **width** is the number $n$ of all wires, including workspace wires. The operation model may also assign weighted gate costs, classical bit costs, and query costs; these are separate coordinates and are summed over the calls actually made.

A workspace wire is an ancilla. A **clean-ancilla promise** specifies computational-basis zero states for the ancillas and requires their exact return for every allowed data input: if $U$ is the implemented unitary, $V_D$ is the declared data unitary, and $|0_A\rangle$ is the specified joint zero vector, then $U(x\otimes|0_A\rangle)=V_Dx\otimes|0_A\rangle$ for every allowed data vector $x$. A **dirty-ancilla promise** permits an arbitrary ancilla state independent of the data input; it may be correlated with an untouched reference. Exact dirty-ancilla restoration means the implemented unitary on data and ancillas is $V_D\otimes I_A$ on the entire joint space, where $V_D$ is the declared unitary on data. The same operator equality then holds after tensoring with the identity on any finite untouched reference. Consequently, product input between the data and the combined ancilla/reference system remains product after the operation. No uncorrelated-output claim is made for an initially data-correlated ancilla.

A controlled or inverse operation is counted only when the operation model explicitly grants that access or supplies a construction; its charge is recorded separately from an ordinary call unless the model explicitly combines them. In particular, the matrix of $U$ alone supplies neither a controlled call nor an inverse query, in accordance with [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]] and [[def-qc-inverse-unitary-access]].

derivations.claim: By [F3], gate budget $C$ counts gate occurrences and $W$ includes every workspace wire. A circuit with $j$ gate occurrences has at most $(AW^k)^j$ ordered gate-list descriptions on $W$ wire labels: there are $A$ gate types and at most $W^k$ ordered supports per type. By [A1], flattening each finite layer list in chronological order preserves its denotation, so every layered circuit of at most $C$ gates is represented by one of these lists. Choosing the designated output wire contributes a factor at most $W$. Thus the number of descriptions is at most $W\sum_{j=0}^{C}(AW^k)^j$. Since $A\ge1$, $W\ge1$, $C\ge n$, and $k$ is fixed, $W=O(C)$ for positive $C$ and $AW^k\ge1$. The sum is at most $(C+1)(AW^k)^C$, whose logarithm is $O(C\log C)$. Duplicate denotations only reduce the number of computed functions.

By [F1], a fixed description has one acceptance probability $p_C(x)$ at each input. If it computed two distinct Boolean functions with success threshold [F2], some input $x$ would require the same number $p_C(x)$ to be both at least $2/3$ and at most $1/3$, which is impossible. Therefore one description accounts for at most one truth table.

There are exactly $2^{2^n}$ Boolean functions on $n$ bits. For $C_n=\lfloor c2^n/n\rfloor$, the bound in step 1.1 has base-two logarithm at most $K C_n\log_2 C_n$ for a constant $K$ depending only on the fixed alphabet and arity. Since $\log_2 C_n\le n+O(1)$, choose $c>0$ so that this logarithm is at most $2^{n-1}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Then the fraction with at most $C_n$ gates is at most $2^{2^{n-1}}/2^{2^n}<0.01$ eventually. By step 1.2, each description covers at most one function, so at least $99\%$ require more than $C_n=\Omega(2^n/n)$ gates. This is an almost-all lower bound, not a lower bound for each named function.

The model in the statement charges the measured output-bit event and includes no free classical postprocessing, so the one-description/one-function count applies as stated. If a classical postprocessing circuit is admitted, it must be included in the finite description and gate count before this argument can be reused.

For sufficiently constructible $t,s\ge\log n$, the VMW model satisfies
$$\mathrm{BQTISP}(t,s)\subseteq\mathrm{PrTISP}_{\rm VMW}(t\,\mathrm{polylog}\,t,s+\mathrm{polylog}\,t).$$
The output is an unbounded-error classical probabilistic simulation in the matching VMW random-access profile; it does not assert conversion to the sequential profile.

For every real $d$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a constant $c>1$ such that at least one of the following holds in the sequential machine profile: $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}\notin\mathrm{PrTIME}_{\rm seq}(n^c)$, or $\mathrm{MajSAT}\notin\mathrm{PrTISP}_{\rm seq}(n^d,n^{1-\varepsilon})$. Formula thresholds are at least-half, and machine acceptance uses strict majority as defined in [[def-qc-unbounded-error-time-space-counting-model]].

Use the fixed multitape fair-bit probabilistic machine interface of [[def-probabilistic-polynomial-time-machine-interface]], with a read-only input tape and charged work tapes. Fix one access profile for each class. In the **sequential** profile, input and work-tape heads move locally, one cell per transition. In the **VMW random-access** profile, the machine has a fixed number of heads; each may move locally, stay put, or jump to an address delimited by two classical work-tape heads. A classical input query reads the addressed input symbol in one transition. If heads collide on a work tape so that its operation is not defined, that tape operation is omitted in that transition. These access profiles define distinct classes and are never silently identified. Time is the worst-case number of transitions on every branch. Sequential-profile space counts distinct visited work cells; VMW-profile space is the maximum work-head address visited on any branch. The read-only input is uncharged.

For a fixed profile and bound t, PrTIME(t) is the class of languages with a machine accepting with probability strictly greater than 1/2 on members and at most 1/2 on nonmembers; PrTISP(t,s) imposes both bounds. We write PrTIME_VMW and PrTISP_VMW when using the VMW random-access profile. Superscript A permits exact classical membership queries to A; writing each query and returning from it are charged, and the total query-string length is bounded by the machine's time. For the sequential profile, LCH_1=PrTIME(n) and LCH_(j+1)=PrTIME(n)^{LCH_j}. An LCH oracle is deterministic: the probabilistic machine's fair-bit branches are external to its oracle queries.

A formula for MajSAT has a fixed finite variable set and is accepted when at least half of all assignments satisfy it. MajMajSAT has two disjoint, ordered variable blocks; for at least half of outer assignments, the residual formula must be true on at least half of the inner assignments. We use at-least-half for both formula thresholds. For real $\theta$ and a real unit vector $\mathbf n=(n_x,n_y,n_z)$, define the axis rotation
